newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Coffee volatility spreads to platinum group.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Coffee volatility spreads to platinum group.

text.p: Recent extreme volatility in coffee prices spread to platinum group metals on Wednesday but although investors were active in both markets it was not seen as part of any concerted move by funds in commodities.
"Both markets have been suffering from supply shortages which is always an attractive scenario for speculators looking for a quick killing," an analyst said.
Other commodity markets were slower affairs with only routine activity noted on the part of the funds.

On the London robusta coffee market the July futures contract fell sharply down through the $2,000 a tonne level as investment funds sought to take some profits from a market which has more than doubled in price since the start of the year.

For the first time in several months some traders were claiming an easing in the supply pipeline, which has been tightly controlled by a producer group, with Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo saying the country was allowing unlimited exports for July and August.

Despite traders being sceptical as to how much coffee exporters in the world's number two coffee producer had available, the news had a markedly dampening effect on previously undented bullish market sentiment.
At the same time Colombian exporters said they noted some resistance to the high prices being asked for June coffee exports.
Meanwhile in the precious metals sector prices one of the smaller volume metals, palladium, swung wildly as leading traders held crisis talks on severe shortages of the metal.
"It's a hairy situation....volatility is huge today," said Nick Moore, analyst at Flemings Global Mining Group.

A combination of a lack of supplies from the world's number one exporter Russia since the start of the year coupled with an investment fund tightly holding on to 1.5 million ounces had created a desperate shortage of the metal.

The scramble to secure supplies, amid fears of the possibility of a default in delivery, had caused the price of the metal to soar to $235 an ounce early Thursday, around double its price earlier this year.

In the industrial metals a more resilient tone was evident after their early-week softening although traders were not convinced a sustained recovery was about to take, given the proximity of the slower third quarter demand period in Europe and the U.S.
Nickel derived some support from the prospect of a lengthy strike at the Western world's number one producer Inco and energy problems at Russia's biggest producer Norilsk.
Zinc shot to a 4-1/2 year high of $1,380 as fears of a flood of surplus Chinese metal into Singapore receded
Market leaders copper and aluminium both staged a rally today but the higher levels attracted selling interest.
